spec_features.spec_quote: If meltdown is detected at iteration 8, we can stop at iteration 10 instead of running all 20
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:230-238: `if iteration_num >= 3 and iteration_num % 3 == 0:` calls `_detect_meltdown`; `if meltdown_conf > 0.6:` sets status='meltdown' and `break`. The break actually terminates the loop, so detection at e.g. iter 9 stops execution before the 20-iter limit.
spec_features.notes: Detection cadence is every 3 iterations (not every iteration), so stop happens at the next multiple-of-3 checkpoint, but it is genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Check for meltdown after every few iterations

spec_features.spec_quote: Global cost budget + per-task iteration limit + wall time limit
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:176-179 global cost check breaks with status 'timeout'; agent_loop.py:182-185 `if time.time() - run_start > (self.iteration_timeout * task_max_iterations): break` (wall time); agent_loop.py:172 `for iteration_num in range(1, task_max_iterations + 1)` caps per-task iterations. All three actually bound execution.
spec_features.notes: All three limits are checked and break/bound the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Check budget ... result.error_message = f"Global budget exceeded: ${self.total_cost_used:.4f}"

spec_features.spec_quote: Check for meltdown midway through task execution, not just at the end
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:230 `if iteration_num >= 3 and iteration_num % 3 == 0:` runs `_detect_meltdown` mid-loop (and a final check at lines 246-252). The mid-loop result is acted on (sets status and breaks at 238), so monitoring occurs during, not only after, execution.
spec_features.notes: Monitoring is wired and its result drives the early stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Check for meltdown after every few iterations

spec_features.feature_name: global cost check before each iteration
spec_features.spec_quote: AgentLoop checks `total_cost_used >= max_global_cost` before each iteration
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:176-179: `if self.total_cost_used >= self.max_global_cost:` at top of the per-iteration loop sets status='timeout' and `break`. total_cost_used is incremented each iteration at line 219, so the comparison is real and acted upon.
